extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent examiners, patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, and parties/petitioners submitting materials to the USPTO
extracted.subtask_description: Procedures and standards in the MPEP for (A) conducting public use/on-sale proceedings (testimony, scheduling, final decision) and (B) submitting, handling, and seeking expungement of trade secret, proprietary, or protective-order materials in patent prosecution and reexamination files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Testimony requirement to establish statutory bar in public use proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The statutory bar (e.g., public use or on-sale under 35 U.S.C. 102(b)) can only be established by testimony taken in accordance with normal rules of evidence, including the right of cross-examination; affidavits or declarations presented with a petition are not to be considered part of the testimony and cannot be used as evidence on behalf of the submitting party unless submitted as part of that party's testimony.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavits/declarations that made out a prima facie case in the petition do not conclusively establish the bar; hearing/testimony procedures should mirror those in an interference, and cross-examination rights must be preserved. See 37 CFR 1.601(b) for affidavit meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scheduling of testimony and filings in public use proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner sets a schedule for taking testimony and for filing the record and briefs using a sequence of closing dates (example items A–F) covering petitioner testimony, applicant objections, petitioner supplemental evidence, requests for cross-examination, cross‑examination, and applicant rebuttal, followed by a schedule for filing records and briefs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example timeline: petitioner testimony close (~60 days after notice); applicant objections (~20 days after that); petitioner supplemental evidence (20 days after objections); applicant request for cross (~20 days later); cross-examination (~30 days later); rebuttal (~20 days later). Filing of record/exhibits and briefs follow (petitioner brief ~30 days after record; applicant brief ~20 days thereafter). Examiners should specify exact dates. No extensions under 37 CFR 1.136(a); petitions to extend final brief time must be under 1.136(b). A certified deposition transcript must be filed within one month (37 CFR 1.678). All papers served per 37 CFR 1.248.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope limitation of testimony in public use proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Testimony in public use proceedings is limited to the issues of public use or on sale; testimony on whether the claimed subject matter would have been obvious over material asserted to be in public use or on sale will not be received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even where final issue may involve obviousness, the testimony record in the public use proceeding must be confined to establishing facts of public use/on-sale; legal conclusions about obviousness are not proper subject of such testimony.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final decision format and content by examiner after public use proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner's final decision should analyze the testimony analogous to a Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences interference decision, state conclusions, and indicate whether a public use or sale bar exists or whether a prima facie case was established and rebutted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner is not bound by any prior prima facie finding. If a bar exists, enter a rejection predicated on the evidence and findings. If not, the written action should nonetheless reflect that 35 U.S.C. 102(b) activity was considered. Use of reasons for allowance under 37 CFR 1.104(e) may be appropriate (see MPEP §1302.14). Petition under 37 CFR 1.181 to vacate will be entertained only for clear error; appellate review under 35 U.S.C. 134 and 141–145 is available once the application returns to ex parte status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to disclose material information regardless of trade secret/proprietary/protective order status
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants and others covered by 37 CFR 1.56(c) and 1.555 must disclose information that is 'material to patentability' to the Office even if it is trade secret, proprietary, or subject to a protective order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Material to patentability defined by 37 CFR 1.56(b): information is material if it is not cumulative and (1) establishes a prima facie case of unpatentability by itself or in combination, or (2) refutes or is inconsistent with a position the applicant takes in opposing unpatentability or asserting patentability. A prima facie case uses the preponderance standard, broadest reasonable construction, and before considering contrary evidence. Trade secret/proprietary status does not negate the disclosure obligation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method of submitting trade secret/proprietary/protective-order materials (MPEP § 724.02)
rubrics_metrics.description: Such materials must be clearly labeled (per-document/item) as 'Trade Secret', 'Proprietary', or 'Subject To Protective Order' and filed in a sealed, clearly labeled envelope or container with complete identifying information and an accompanying transmittal letter stating the status and citing MPEP § 724.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use terms like 'Restricted' or 'Confidential' (avoids confusion with national security markings). If 'Subject To Protective Order', identify the tribunal, case number, date of order, and proceeding status on each document. A petition under 37 CFR 1.59 with fee (37 CFR 1.17(h)) to expunge may accompany the submission. Prefer hand-carry to the relevant Technology Center/TC Director's office; mailing is permitted but less desirable to avoid mishandling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of materials appropriate for submission under MPEP § 724.02
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions under § 724.02 contemplate information 'material to patentability' (i.e., adverse material), and do not include information favorable to patentability (e.g., commercial success evidence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not submit favorable-to-patentability evidence under § 724.02; if trade‑secret/proprietary materials are included in amendments, arguments, or affidavits (§1.131/1.132), they will be made of record with no special status. Protestor submissions may be made under § 724.02 before application publication if protestor has access; after publication protests require applicant consent. Parties served cannot be guaranteed to keep material secret; comments should avoid disclosing details or be submitted separately under § 724.02.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office handling: determination of 'important to a reasonable examiner' and treatment of submitted materials (MPEP § 724.04)
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receipt the USPTO date-stamps the transmittal and notes on the application that trade secret/proprietary/protective-order material has been filed and where located. The examiner or responsible official will determine whether any portion is 'important to a reasonable examiner' in deciding patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If found important: cite in next Office action (becomes part of file history and public upon patent issuance). If found not important: next Office action will indicate such without including details; the material will be resealed and retained pending any petition to expunge. Materials are maintained in original sealed container marked 'Not Open To The Public' while determinations/petitions are pending. Specific procedures vary slightly for original applications (35 U.S.C. 122), reissue applications (37 CFR 1.11(b)), and reexamination files (37 CFR 1.11(d))—see subsection-specific A–G rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of materials submitted in applications covered by 35 U.S.C. 122 (pre/post publication)
rubrics_metrics.description: Materials submitted under § 724.02 in applications covered by 35 U.S.C. 122 are maintained in original sealed container and not publicly available while pending; after publication they should not be made available to members of the public requesting the file wrapper while the application remains pending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the published application is later abandoned and no petition to expunge was filed, materials become available to the public under 37 CFR 1.14(c) or (e). If found important they will be cited and become part of file history; if not, they are resealed and retained pending petition to expunge. Petitions to expunge treated per MPEP § 724.05.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of materials submitted in reissue applications and reexamination files open to the public
rubrics_metrics.description: Materials submitted under § 724.02 in reissue applications or reexamination files that are open to the public are kept separate from the public file and not made publicly available until a determination is made about their importance to a reasonable examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If deemed important they will be cited and become a permanent part of the application/reexamination file and open to the public; if not important they will be resealed, retained separate from the file, and unavailable to the public pending petition to expunge. Pending petitions, sealed containers must be clearly marked 'Not Open To The Public'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents and timing of a petition to expunge information submitted under MPEP § 724.02 (MPEP § 724.05, I)
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition under 37 CFR 1.59(b) to expunge information submitted under § 724.02 will be entertained only if the petition fee (37 CFR 1.17(h)) is filed and the information has been found not to be important to a reasonable examiner; such petition must include specific items (A–E).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required petition contents: (A) clear identification of information to be expunged without disclosing details; (B) statement that the information is trade secret/proprietary/subject to protective order and not otherwise public; (C) commitment to retain such information for the period of any patent for which it was submitted; (D) statement that the petition is submitted by/on behalf of the party in interest who originally submitted the information; (E) fee (37 CFR 1.17(i)). Petitions should accompany the submission and be timely so they can be acted on prior to abandonment or issuance. Decision will often be held in abeyance until close of prosecution or abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitions to expunge unintentionally submitted information (MPEP § 724.05, II)
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition to expunge information unintentionally submitted in an application (not part of original disclosure) may be filed under 37 CFR 1.59(b) if specific conditions (A–F) are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required conditions: (A) the Office can return the information prior to issuance of any patent; (B) statement that submission was inadvertent and failure to return would cause irreparable harm; (C) the information has not been made public; (D) commitment to retain the information for the period of any patent for which it was submitted; (E) it is established to the Commissioner's satisfaction that the information is not material under 37 CFR 1.56; (F) petition fee (37 CFR 1.17(h)). Unidentified information not separately marked may be placed in the examiner's prior art search file and not retrievable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitions to expunge papers submitted in incorrect application (MPEP § 724.05, III)
rubrics_metrics.description: When papers were placed in the wrong application file (e.g., wrong heading), a petition should request return (not transfer) of the papers; grant governed by factors in subsection II.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Office can determine the correct application based on headings (application number, filing date, title, inventor), the Office will transfer the papers to the correct file without petition. Otherwise requests for return are evaluated under the unintentionally submitted standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expungement of information forming part of the original disclosure (MPEP § 724.05, IV)
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition to expunge information that forms part of the original disclosure (specification, claims, drawings, prelim. amendments included in oath/declaration) must be filed under 37 CFR 1.183; such petitions ordinarily will not be favorably entertained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Granting such a petition requires waiver of 37 CFR 1.59(a) and would require changing the USPTO record of the originally filed application (scanned into record), which may not be possible. Direct these petitions to the Office of Petitions and explain why justice requires waiver.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of petitions to expunge (MPEP § 724.06)
rubrics_metrics.description: Expungement is not available for original disclosure; petitions under 37 CFR 1.59(b) must include required fee and establish appropriateness to Commissioner's satisfaction. Return of information originally submitted under § 724.02 is appropriate when the petition satisfies the specific MPEP requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If information was not submitted under § 724.02 or as an IDS, petitions should be sent to the Office of Petitions. Decision on petitions is generally held in abeyance until allowance, Ex parte Quayle action, or Notice of Abandonment, at which time petition will be decided; except where it is clear the information was filed in the wrong application, in which case a prompt decision should be made. Form paragraph 7.204 provides template language for holding petition decision in abeyance.
